title: Pollen-grain shape depends on whether walls harden before the tetrad separates

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Pollen-grain shape depends on whether walls harden before the tetrad separates

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Pollen grains and spores formed as tetrahedral tetrads keep the plane facets and sharp angles of the tetrad if their walls solidify before the grains separate, but become spherical if they separate while still soft.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. VIII: The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates (continued)

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: the pollen-grains afterwards fall apart, and their individual form will depend upon whether or no their walls have solidified before this liberation takes place.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter VIII, “The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates (continued)”; topic “Tetrads of pollen and spores”. Scope: pollen grains of angiosperms and spores of ferns and red algae formed in tetrads

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch08-14: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.67

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The predicted shape contrast is readily measurable and pollen databases provide broad comparative material. Existing data only partly connect final geometry to the crucial temporal ordering of wall solidification and liberation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Relate mature pollen or spore sphericity and retained tetrad facets to evidence for wall maturation timing relative to separation across taxa and developmental image series.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Mature shape alone cannot establish wall-hardening time.

Developmental series and mature morphology are rarely linked for the same taxa.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

analysis feasibility: 0.7
operationalizability: 0.88
data existence: 0.66
discriminating power: 0.64

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Pollen shape and tetrad versus monad status are openly coded for a large angiosperm sample, which proxies the claim by asking whether retained tetrads are the faceted grains. The actual timing of solidification is in scattered ultrastructural studies, not in PalDat. Shape has several other causes, so the association is informative and confounded.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare mature pollen and spore shape with whether the wall rigidified before the tetrad separated. Grains that hardened in the tetrad keeping plane facets and sharp angles, and grains that separated while soft becoming spherical, would support the claim; spherical grains that hardened in permanent tetrads, or angular grains that separated soft, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Apertures, harmomegathy and drying also produce facets, and fern and red-algal spores are outside this pollen database.

PalDat records shape and whether grains are united, not the developmental timing of wall hardening relative to separation.
